justification: One URL added to the sitemap plus a test that reads the filesystem to stop the omission recurring. No component, API, query or served value changes. Not minor-by-size alone: the accompanying claims audit of the page found nothing to correct, so the diff really is two files.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A directory under app/for/ contains a page.tsx whose route is absent from app/sitemap.ts. It reads the FILESYSTEM rather than a second hardcoded list, because a hardcoded list would drift from the first one in exactly the way that caused this.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Deleting the /for/students line from sitemap.ts: 1 failed, 7 passed. The seven that pass are the other audiences, so the test discriminates rather than failing wholesale. With the line present: 8 passed.

pre_impl.existing_data: No database. Two filesystem sources: the directories under frontend-nextjs/app/for/ that contain a page.tsx, and the URL list in frontend-nextjs/app/sitemap.ts. Seven audience pages exist on disk; six were listed.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The assumption worth testing was the page's own numbers, since the email being drafted rests on them. Both hold: '28 councils have numeric controls' — 28 actual councils (29 counting nsw_statewide, which is not a council); 'roughly one citation in thirteen does not resolve to a clause' — 75 of 967 refs carry no digit locator, 1 in 12.9. Nothing on the page needed correcting, so nothing was changed.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies at the next build; sitemaps are generated per request from this list. Nothing is backfilled. The page itself is untouched and has been live throughout.

break_it.scenario: A /for/ audience page ships and is never added to the sitemap.
break_it.what_happens: The page is live and no search engine is told it exists. /for/students sat in none of the 8 sitemap chunks from the day it was built. Six of seven pages being listed made the omission look exactly like a complete list.
break_it.how: frontend-nextjs/__tests__/sitemap-covers-for-pages.test.ts enumerates app/for/*/page.tsx from disk and asserts each route string appears in sitemap.ts.
break_it.repro: Delete the /for/students line and run the test: 1 failed, 7 passed

break_it.scenario: The guard stops finding pages and passes vacuously.
break_it.what_happens: A directory rename or a move of app/for/ would make the enumeration empty, every parametrised assertion would vanish, and the suite would go green while checking nothing — the exact shape of a check that quietly stops checking.
break_it.how: A separate assertion requires the discovered audience list to be non-empty before the per-audience checks are trusted.
break_it.repro: Point FOR_DIR at an empty directory and the 'finds the audience pages at all' test fails first
